whyEn: The last chapter of the book answers the question BC's practical stations open with every single time: 'Is the scene safe?' — and gives it real content beyond a ritual phrase. It tests three decision skills: when NOT to enter (staging before the scene is secured, reading a dark silent house, approaching a stopped vehicle), when to get OUT (cover versus concealment, retreat triggers), and how to treat a patient inside a crime scene without wrecking the investigation (one path in and out, cut around bullet and knife holes, touch nothing you do not have to, document what you moved). Weight is low — one written question or one scene-safety checkpoint — but the entry/retreat logic also props up the behavioural, abuse, and tactical questions scattered through the rest of the exam.
whyZh: 全书最后一章，回答的正是BC实操考每一站开场必问的那句『现场安全吗？』——把这句仪式性的话变成有血有肉的判断标准。它考三种决策能力：什么时候不进（现场未被控制前在外staging、如何解读一栋漆黑无声的房子、如何接近一辆停着的车）；什么时候撤（掩体与隐蔽物的区别、触发撤离的信号）；以及如何在犯罪现场里救人又不毁掉侦查（进出走同一条路、剪衣服绕开弹孔刀口、能不碰的都不碰、动过什么如实记录）。权重不高——笔试一两题或实操一个安全检查点——但这套进入/撤离逻辑同时支撑着行为急症、虐待、战术场景等散落全卷的题目。

areas: Area 8: Health Care Promotion and Public Safety

sections.titleEn: Introduction: No Such Thing as a Routine Call

points.en: There is no 'normal' call — a welfare check can put you in front of a confused man with a weapon at his bedside, an injury call can drop you into a live domestic fight, and a rally first-aid stop can surround you with violent protestors. Situational awareness has to run on every call, not just the ones dispatch flags as dangerous.
points.zh: 不存在『普通』的出勤——上门查看独居老人，可能撞上一个床边放着武器、把你当成入侵者的糊涂人；处理受伤呼叫，可能一脚踏进正在动手的家庭纠纷；在集会现场做急救，可能被暴力示威者包围。情境意识必须在每一次出勤中全程在线，而不是只在调度标注『危险』的呼叫里才打开。

points.en: The core doctrine of the whole chapter: once you recognize a violent situation, your goal is to retreat to a safe location and wait for law enforcement — managing the violence is police work, not paramedic work. Paramedics have been seriously injured and killed trying to reach patients through violent scenes, which is why the book urges you to push your agency for self-protection courses built for emergency responders.
points.zh: 全章的核心信条：一旦识别出暴力局面，你的目标是撤到安全位置、等待警方到场——处置暴力是警察的工作，不是救护员的工作。已有救护员在穿越暴力现场救人的过程中重伤甚至殉职，所以原书敦促你推动所在机构开设面向急救人员的自我保护课程。

sections.titleEn: Awareness: Reading Danger Before It Reads You
sections.titleZh: 危险意识：在危险发现你之前先发现它

points.en: Violence is not an urban phenomenon — a rural call can be just as deadly, and in many rural areas the paramedic arrives long before police do, making you your own first line of scene security. Use the drive to prepare mentally and talk options through with your partner; on arrival do a scene assessment focused on your own safety first. If the scene feels unsafe, call for police and stage until they secure it — a paramedic injured by rushing in becomes one more casualty complicating the scene for everyone behind them.
points.zh: 暴力不是大城市的专利——乡村呼叫同样可能致命，而且在许多乡村地区，救护员比警察早到很久，最初的现场安全只能靠你自己把关。利用赶往现场的路上做心理预案、和搭档讨论几种应对方案；到场后先做一次以自身安全为核心的现场评估。感觉现场不安全，就呼叫警方并在外等待其控制现场——贸然冲进去受伤的救护员，只会变成又一名伤员，给搭档和后续力量添乱。

points.en: Paramedic uniforms — badge, shoulder patch, collar insignia, name plate — look enough like police uniforms that aggression meant for law enforcement lands on you instead. The fix many agencies use: high-visibility uniforms with the service logo and PARAMEDIC printed large across the shirt.
points.zh: 救护员制服上的徽章、臂章、领章、姓名牌与警服相似度很高，冲着警察去的敌意会误落到你头上。许多机构的对策是改用高可见度制服：印上机构标志，胸前再加超大号 PARAMEDIC 字样。

points.en: Soft body armour comes in five protection levels and is not necessarily bulletproof; it never covers the neck or head, so you stay vulnerable no matter the level. The book's verdict: sound survival skills that keep you out of dangerous situations protect you more than any vest.
points.zh: 软质防弹衣共分五个防护等级，且未必真能挡住所有子弹；它永远护不到颈部和头部，所以无论穿哪一级都仍有要害暴露。原书的结论：让你根本不落入险境的生存技能，比任何防弹衣都更能保命。

points.en: Dispatch nature predicts violence: a shooting, stabbing, or attempted suicide call should raise your guard before you arrive. On 'routine' sick calls, watch for the early tells — abnormal behaviour, threatening body positioning, harsh language — and move yourself, your team, and if possible the patient to safety before words become blows. The named failure mode is tunnel vision: becoming so absorbed in patient care that you stop seeing the threat building around you.
points.zh: 呼叫性质本身能预告暴力：枪击、捅刺、自杀未遂类呼叫在到场前就该拉高警戒。而在『普通』的伤病呼叫里，要盯住暴力的早期信号——异常举止、带威胁性的站位、粗暴的语言——在动口升级为动手之前，把自己、团队、可能的话连同患者一起转移到安全处。这里点名的失败模式叫『隧道视野』：一头扎进救治里，对身边正在酝酿的威胁视而不见。

points.en: Agencies write SOPs for predictable danger scenes — drug labs, civil disturbances, hostage or barricade incidents — including which scenes require staging and how far away. Treat SOPs like standing orders: your default playbook, but modifiable when following them would cost you or your partner's life. Read the SOP manual when you take the job, not after your first bad call.
points.zh: 机构会为可预见的危险场景制定标准作业程序（SOP）——毒品制造窝点、群体骚乱、劫持或据守事件——包括哪类现场必须在外staging、要停多远。对待SOP要像对待standing orders：默认照做，但当照做会危及你或搭档性命时可以变通。入职时就该读完SOP手册，而不是等第一次出事之后。

sections.titleZh: 公路事件：接近停驶车辆的战术

points.en: 'Man slumped over the steering wheel' and 'unresponsive person in a vehicle' are classic trap calls — the occupant may be drunk, drugged, or armed, and your police-lookalike uniform makes an impaired occupant more likely to react to you as a threat.
points.zh: 『有人趴在方向盘上』『车内有人叫不醒』是经典的陷阱型呼叫——车内的人可能醉酒、嗑药或持有武器，而你那身酷似警服的制服，会让神志不清的人更容易把你当成威胁来对付。

points.en: First unit on a stopped-vehicle call: park a minimum of 6 m behind the vehicle, angled 10 degrees toward the driver's side with your nose facing the shoulder, front wheels cranked fully left — that geometry puts your wheels and engine block between you and any gunfire from the car.
points.zh: 首车抵达停驶车辆现场的停车法：停在目标车后方至少6米处，车身向驾驶员一侧偏10度、车头朝路肩，前轮向左打死——这个几何布局让你的车轮和发动机缸体挡在你与车内可能射来的子弹之间。

points.en: Arriving after others: ask the incident commander where to park, or default to parking downstream of the wreck; police cars and fire engines deliberately park behind the crashed vehicle to act as a crash buffer against inattentive drivers.
points.zh: 非首车到场：先问事故指挥官（IC）把车停哪，默认停在事故点的下游侧；警车和消防车会故意停在事故车后方，充当挡住走神来车的缓冲屏障。

points.en: After dark, use high beams and spotlights to flood the target vehicle — bright light both exposes the interior and hides your approach. Never walk between the spotlight and the car: you would cast a silhouette straight into the occupant's rear-view mirror. Same logic rules your flashlight: keep it off until needed, hold it at arm's length away from your body, and light the scene only a few seconds at a time — a lit flashlight is an aiming point you do not want centred on your chest.
points.zh: 夜间用远光灯和探照灯把目标车照透——强光既照亮车内，也掩护你的接近。但绝不要从探照灯与目标车之间走过：你的剪影会直接投进车内人的后视镜里。手电也遵循同一逻辑：不到需要时不开，开灯时手臂伸直、让灯远离躯干，每次只照几秒——亮着的手电就是瞄准点，你不会想让它正对着自己的胸口。

points.en: Before anyone leaves the unit, radio dispatch with the situation, location, and the plate number and province — if things go wrong mid-approach, dispatch already knows where to send help. Some services flatly prohibit approaching a vehicle until police arrive; know your local policy.
points.zh: 任何人下车之前，先用电台向调度报告状况、位置、车牌号及其所属省份——万一接近过程中出事，调度已经知道往哪派援。有的机构干脆规定警察未到场前禁止接近车辆；务必弄清本地政策。

points.en: Only one person approaches: the paramedic in the right front seat (the vehicle's IC) makes the walk-up while everyone else stays with the unit. Route: to the rear passenger-side trunk area first — check the trunk lid is properly shut because people can hide inside, and if the trunk is open, retreat to your vehicle.
points.zh: 只派一个人接近：坐在右前座的救护员（本车IC）负责走向目标车，其余人全部留在救护车上。路线：先到目标车右后方后备箱区——检查后备箱盖是否关严，因为里面可能藏人；后备箱开着就直接撤回车上。

points.en: Advance belly-in (pressed toward the car body, minimizing your visible profile) to the passenger-side C column and stop. Through the rear and side glass: count occupants and fixate on their hands — every stab, strike, or shot starts with a hand. Scan for guns and knives but also bats, beer bottles, tire irons, and pipe. Deadly weapon seen or suspected: retreat and call police; officers are trained to secure weapons, paramedics are not, and you never attempt to unload one.
points.zh: 以『贴身』方式（belly-in，身体紧贴车身、把暴露轮廓压到最小）前移到副驾一侧的C柱停住。透过后窗和侧窗：数清车内人数，死盯他们的手——捅、打、开枪，动作全从手开始。既要找枪和刀，也要留意球棒、酒瓶、轮胎撬棍、铁管。看到或怀疑有致命武器：撤退并呼叫警方；警察受过收缴武器的训练，救护员没有，而且永远不要尝试给武器退弹。

points.en: The C column is the decision line: if the back seat is occupied, do not pass it — passing puts the rear passengers behind your back and splits your attention. Back seat empty: belly-in to the B column, read the front seats, then tap the window and announce 'Paramedic. Do you need help?' — without ever stepping past the B column into the driver's-door area police call the kill zone.
points.zh: C柱就是决策线：后排有人就绝不越过C柱——一旦越过，后排乘客就到了你背后，你的注意力被迫前后分裂。后排没人：继续贴身前移到B柱，看清前排状况，然后敲窗表明身份：『救护员，需要帮助吗？』——但脚步永远不跨过B柱进入驾驶门区，那是警察口中的『杀伤区』（kill zone）。

points.en: Flashlight discipline: keep it off until needed, hold it at arm's length away from your body when you switch it on, and light the scene only a few seconds at a time — a lit flashlight is an aiming point, and you do not want it centred on your chest.
points.zh: 手电纪律：不到需要时不开，开灯时手臂伸直、让灯远离躯干，每次只照几秒——亮着的手电就是瞄准点，你不会想让它正对着自己的胸口。

points.en: Vans get a modified approach: you cannot see the cargo, which could be a crowd of people or a stack of weapons, and the sliding side door can fly open and pull you in. Stay 3 to 5 m off the passenger side, walk parallel to the van, and only close in once you are about 45 degrees forward of the A column — the one spot with maximum view inside at a still-safe distance.
points.zh: 厢式车要用改良接近法：你看不见货舱里装的是什么——可能是一车人，也可能是一堆武器——而且侧滑门可能突然拉开把你拽进去。全程与副驾一侧保持3到5米距离、平行于车身走，直到走到A柱前方约45度角的位置才收拢距离——那是既能最大限度看清车内、又仍在安全距离上的唯一站位。

points.en: Retreat doctrine: backing away and calling for police is the safest exit. If your partner goes down mid-approach, do not run to them — back off and make the call, because summoning help fast is what actually saves them. The bare-minimum distress message is your unit identifier plus your current location; the full report adds number of aggressors, number and type of injuries and weapons, the vehicle's make, colour, body style and plate, and its direction of travel if it flees. Then document in detail why you left the scene.
points.zh: 撤退信条：后退脱离并呼叫警方是最安全的退出方式。搭档在接近途中倒下时，不要冲上去——先退开、发出呼救，因为让援兵尽快到场才是真正能救他的事。最低限度的求援信息是本车编号加当前位置；完整报告再加上袭击者人数、伤员数量与伤情、武器数量与类型、涉事车辆的品牌/颜色/车型/车牌，以及它逃离时的去向。事后详细记录你为什么撤离现场。

sections.titleEn: Residential Incidents: Doorways, Exits, and the Fatal Funnel
sections.titleZh: 住宅事件：门口、退路与『致命漏斗』

points.en: Residential violence hides inside routine calls: a post-seizure patient may be confused enough to pull the handgun from under his pillow, and an intoxicated relative distraught over a loved one's illness can turn on the crew mid-treatment. Every dwelling call carries violence potential, and reassessment continues throughout care.
points.zh: 住宅暴力常藏在普通呼叫里：癫痫发作后意识模糊的患者可能从枕头底下摸出手枪；因亲人病情而醉酒失态的家属可能在你救治中途对你动手。每一趟入户呼叫都自带暴力可能，安全评估要贯穿救治全程。

points.en: Walk-up protocol: one paramedic approaches the house while the partner hangs back a short distance — a free partner is your lifeline to call for help if violence erupts. On approach, listen for loud or threatening voices, glance through windows, look for visible weapons; perceive danger and you back off to the unit, call police, and wait.
points.zh: 接近住宅的规程：一名救护员上前，搭档在稍远处停住——留在外围的搭档就是暴力爆发时能呼救的那根生命线。接近途中留意屋内有无高声或威胁性的叫喊，扫一眼能看到的窗户，寻找可见的武器；一旦察觉危险，退回车上、呼叫警方、原地等待。

points.en: The doorway is the 'fatal funnel' — the spot where you are easiest to see and hardest to move out of, and most bullets punch straight through anything short of the heaviest doors. Approach off the main front-door path; at the door stand on the doorknob side (from the hinge side, an occupant can watch you through a barely opened door while you see almost nothing inside), then knock and announce 'Paramedics' so nobody mistakes you for police.
points.zh: 门口就是『致命漏斗』——你在那里最容易被看见、又最难闪开，而且大多数子弹能轻松穿透除最厚重者外的任何门板。接近时避开正对大门的主通道；到门前站在门把手一侧（若站在铰链一侧，屋里的人只需把门开一条缝就能看清你，而你几乎看不见屋内），然后敲门并喊出『救护员』，免得被误认成警察。

points.en: Ask whoever answers the door to lead you to the patient: you reach the patient faster, the guide doubles as a shield, and their reaction buys you moments of warning if things sour. Dark house? Have the guide turn the lights on so you are not fighting at a low-light disadvantage.
points.zh: 请开门的人带你去患者身边：一来找得快，二来带路人本身是道人肉屏障，三来他的反应能在局面恶化时给你几秒预警。屋里没开灯？让带路人把灯打开，别让自己吃低光照的亏。

points.en: Inside any structure, name your exits: a primary exit (normally the door you came in through) and a secondary exit (a rear door or a window), and keep at least one escape route accessible the whole time you are in the building.
points.zh: 进入任何建筑都要先定好退路：一条主退路（通常就是你进来的那扇门），一条备用退路（后门或窗户），并且在楼内的整段时间里，始终保证至少一条逃生通道随时可用。

points.en: At the patient's room, sweep for weapons before you kneel down. A gun or knife in view means backing out of the residence and calling police. Also clock the improvised arsenal — ashtrays, scissors, bottles, fireplace pokers, knitting needles — and move anything usable as a weapon out of the patient's reach.
points.zh: 到达患者所在房间，先扫一遍武器再蹲下救治。看见枪或刀，就倒退出屋、呼叫警方。同时留意那些临时武器——烟灰缸、剪刀、瓶子、壁炉拨火棍、织毛衣的针——把一切可能当武器的东西挪出患者伸手可及的范围。

points.en: A violent or physical domestic dispute in progress means you do not enter until police arrive. Emotions on these scenes boiled over before you got there: avoid confrontational words or actions that reignite them. Your voice — tone, pace, pitch, professional and respectful — is the single most effective tool for staying out of trouble in a dispute.
points.zh: 到场时家庭纠纷仍在动手，就等警察到了再进门。这类现场的情绪在你抵达前就已沸腾：避免任何可能再点燃它的对抗性言行。你的声音——语气、语速、音调，专业而尊重——是纠纷现场让你置身事外的最有效工具。

points.en: Crisis intervention is not the paramedic's job — you are not a marriage counsellor, psychologist, or clergy member. What is your job: knowing your jurisdiction's mandatory reporting duties, since most provinces and territories now have civil legislation protecting women in domestic violence situations (full domestic-violence assessment lives in Chapter 46).
points.zh: 危机干预不是救护员的活——你不是婚姻顾问、心理学家或神职人员。属于你的活是：弄清所在辖区的强制报告义务，因为加拿大大多数省和地区已通过保护家暴处境中妇女的民事立法（家暴的完整评估内容见第46章）。

sections.titleEn: Violence on the Streets: Drug Labs, Gangs, Shooters, Hostages
sections.titleZh: 街头暴力：制毒窝点、帮派、枪手与人质

points.en: A clandestine drug lab can be built for a few hundred dollars, and it comes in three flavours — chemical-reaction labs (classically methamphetamine: street names meth, speed, crank), extraction labs pulling product from raw materials, and grow labs raising marijuana. The tells when nothing says 'lab': bulk over-the-counter cold remedies containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine, gallon containers of camping fuel, and lye (sulfuric acid). Nearly every chemical on site is a hazardous material, many flammable or toxic — and cookers add booby traps: fragmentation and incendiary devices, animal traps, impaling stakes.
points.zh: 一个地下制毒窝点几百加元就能搭起来，形态分三类——化学反应型（典型产物是冰毒，街头叫 meth、speed、crank）、从原料里提取成品的萃取型、种植大麻的种植型。当现场看不出『实验室』样子时，认出它靠这些破绽：成堆的含麻黄碱/伪麻黄碱非处方感冒药、成加仑的野营燃料、碱液（硫酸）。现场几乎每种化学品都是危险物质，多数易燃或有毒——制毒者还会布设诡雷：破片和燃烧装置、捕兽夹、穿刺尖桩。

points.en: Recognize a lab and your job becomes staying clear until trained police and hazmat specialists secure it. Touch nothing. Take patients out with you only if removal does not expose you and your team to more hazardous material.
points.zh: 一旦确认是制毒窝点，你的任务就变成：远离现场，等受训警察和危险品专家控制局面。什么都别碰。只有在撤离不会让你和团队多吸一口危险品的前提下，才把患者一并带出去。

points.en: Canadian gang math: gang-related homicides climbed from 4% of all homicides in 1994 to 25% in 2016, and gangs have spread from big cities into suburban and rural communities. Gang culture runs on three Rs — Reputation (earned by crime), Respect (often really fear), Retaliation (mandatory whenever the gang is 'dissed' by graffiti, hand signs, hard stares, or social media posts).
points.zh: 加拿大的帮派数字：帮派相关凶杀占全部凶杀的比例从1994年的4%攀升到2016年的25%，帮派也早已从大城市蔓延到郊区和乡村。帮派文化靠『三个R』运转——名声（Reputation，靠犯罪挣来）、尊重（Respect，实质常是恐惧）、报复（Retaliation，只要被涂鸦、手势、瞪视或社交媒体帖子『不敬』，就必须报复）。

points.en: Working gang territory: never flash gang signs or slang even if you know them — you are not a member, and imitation reads as mockery. In gang strongholds, take police escorts for all medical calls. For a drive-by shooting victim, keep open-air treatment to a minimum and get the patient into the ambulance fast: a visible patient invites the second volley.
points.zh: 在帮派地盘干活的规矩：就算你懂帮派手势和黑话也绝不能用——你不是成员，模仿等于挑衅。在帮派据点区域，所有医疗呼叫都应请警方护送。处理驾车枪击的伤者时，露天救治压到最少、尽快把人抬进救护车：暴露在外的患者就是第二轮扫射的靶子。

points.en: Mass-shooting geometry: units hold in staging until police secure the scene, and staging, treatment, and triage areas may need to sit as far as 2 km out — always placed out of line-of-sight (hence line-of-fire) from windows. School parking lots and playing fields look like perfect staging but hand a shooter a wide-open field of fire. The only medics who work inside hostile ground are tactical paramedics — specially trained, embedded with SWAT/mobile response teams to treat officers, barricaded patients, and hostages — a role nobody improvises into.
points.zh: 大规模枪击现场的几何学：救护单位在staging区待命直到警方控制现场，而staging、治疗与检伤分类区可能要设在远至2公里之外——并且一律避开来自窗户的视线（即射线）。学校停车场和操场看似完美的集结地，实际上正好给枪手送上开阔的射界。唯一在敌对区域内工作的医护是战术救护员——受过专门训练、随SWAT/机动响应队行动，救治警员、据守中的患者和人质——这个角色没人能临场客串。

points.en: Cover stops bullets; concealment only hides you. Cover: trees, utility poles, mail-collection boxes, dumpsters, curbs, vehicles, dips in the ground. Concealment: tall grass, shrubbery, dark shadow. Doctrine when fire erupts: grab concealment if no cover is at hand while you read your position, then work toward cover and stay there until the scene is secure or you can retreat.
points.zh: 掩体（cover）挡得住子弹；隐蔽物（concealment）只藏得住身影。掩体：树干、电线杆、邮筒、垃圾大箱、路缘石、车辆、地面凹陷。隐蔽物：高草、灌木、暗影。枪响时的信条：手边没有掩体就先用隐蔽物藏身、判断处境，然后设法转移到掩体后面，守到现场被控制或找到撤退机会为止。

points.en: Hostage numbers and stages: most Canadian hostage incidents run 4.5 to 5 hours, and the event unfolds in six stages — surveillance, capture, transport, holding, move, resolution — with the captured paramedic hit hardest by capture, transport, and holding. Time is your ally: survival odds rise steadily from capture to release, because a live hostage stays useful as a bargaining chip.
points.zh: 人质事件的数字与阶段：加拿大多数人质事件持续4.5到5小时，全程分六个阶段——侦察、劫持、转移、扣押、再转移、解决——被劫持的救护员受冲击最大的是劫持、转移、扣押三段。时间站在你这边：从被劫到获释，生存几率随时间稳步上升，因为活着的人质才是有用的谈判筹码。

points.en: Hostage survival playbook: do not attempt escape (a failed try makes every hostage's position worse); swallow the instinctive anger of being grabbed; follow instructions on the assumption the gun will be used. If moved while blindfolded, work your senses — sounds, smells of animals, chemicals or food, stair counts, number of captors — it all becomes police intelligence after release.
points.zh: 人质生存手册：不要尝试逃跑（一次失败的尝试会让所有人质的处境更糟）；咽下被人抓住时的本能怒火；按指令行事，并默认对方真的会开枪。被蒙眼转移时调动所有感官——声音，动物、化学品或食物的气味，走了几层楼梯，绑匪有几个人——这些在获释后全是警方的情报。

points.en: In the holding stage your own mind is a bigger threat than the captors: stay inconspicuous, never stare, and strip the authority image off your uniform — remove badge, collar pins, and patches, or wear the shirt inside out, because other hostages looking to you for leadership marks you as a threat. Ask to treat the wounded, captors included: it keeps your mind working, reads as nonthreatening, raises your value, and is exactly what your code of ethics says anyway. After release, seek professional counselling even if you feel fine — hostages can develop posttraumatic stress disorder, and the psychological toll routinely outweighs the physical one.
points.zh: 扣押阶段，你自己的心态比绑匪更危险：保持低调、绝不盯着绑匪看，并卸掉制服上的权威符号——摘下徽章、领章、臂章，或把制服反穿，因为其他人质把你当主心骨的样子，在绑匪眼里就是威胁。主动请求救治伤者，包括绑匪本人：这让你的头脑保持运转、显得无害、抬高你的价值——而且这本来就是职业伦理的要求。获释后即使自我感觉良好，也要寻求专业心理辅导——人质经历可能发展成创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），心理创伤通常远比身体伤害更重。

sections.titleEn: Contact and Cover: Making Yourself Hard to Hit
sections.titleZh: 接触与掩护：让自己难以被击中

points.en: The paramedic patch is not a shield: assume anyone holding a weapon will harm whoever is in sight, uniform or not. If you see police officers diving for cover, that is your cue — take cover in the immediate vicinity and mould your body to the shape of the object.
points.zh: 救护员的臂章不是护身符：默认持武器的人会伤害视线内的任何人，穿不穿制服都一样。看到警察在找掩体卧倒，那就是给你的信号——立即在附近寻找掩体，并让身体尽量贴合掩体的外形。

points.en: Against an elevated shooter (upper window, rooftop), a wall or car roof leaves your head and upper torso exposed from above. Use the engine block and wheel areas of a vehicle as cover, stay away from the fuel tank — and never tuck between the wheels, because a skilled shooter can ricochet rounds off the pavement in front of you into that space.
points.zh: 面对高处的枪手（楼上窗口、屋顶），普通墙体或车顶挡不住俯视视角，你的头和上半身会从掩体上沿露出来。要用车辆的发动机缸体和车轮部位作掩体，远离油箱——并且绝不要钻到两轮之间的车底，因为老练的射手能让子弹在你面前的路面上跳弹打进那个空间。

points.en: A fire hydrant is legitimate last-resort cover: your arm, knee, or shoulder may take a hit, but your central body mass and vital organs are protected — and that still beats standing in the open.
points.zh: 消防栓是合格的保底掩体：手臂、膝盖、肩膀可能中弹，但躯干核心和要害器官有遮挡——这仍然远好过站在空地上挨枪。

points.en: Indoor cover audit: a solid oak desk or a refrigerator can stop or deflect a bullet — that is cover; a sofa or stuffed chair merely hides you — that is concealment. The same test applies to walls: brick and concrete-block stop rounds, porous cinder block does not absorb a bullet's energy, and interior stud-and-drywall walls are concealment only.
points.zh: 室内掩体审查：实心橡木桌、冰箱能挡住或偏转子弹——算掩体；沙发、软垫椅只能藏住身影——只算隐蔽物。墙也用同一标准检验：砖墙和混凝土砌块墙挡得住子弹，多孔的煤渣砖吸收不了子弹的能量，而室内龙骨加石膏板的隔墙只提供隐蔽。

points.en: Trapped behind a frame wall? Stand at the door or window frames — those lines carry extra framing lumber, the most bullet-resistant wood in the wall.
points.zh: 只能躲在木框架隔墙后面时，站到门框或窗框的位置——那里为承重加了额外的框料，是整面墙里木料最厚、最挡子弹的部位。

points.en: Relocate only when all three conditions hold: the new spot is better cover, it is farther from the hostility, and you can reach it without exposing yourself. Scout first with the quick-peek technique — several brief looks from behind cover, each from a different height and angle, returning to cover fast — never a long stare from one spot. And when you do move, never run straight away from the shooter: run a zigzag, because movement across the assailant's field of view is far harder to hit than movement along the line of fire.
points.zh: 换位置必须同时满足三个条件：新位置掩护更好、离敌意源更远、转移途中不暴露自己。转移前先用『快速探视』侦察——从掩体后短促地探看几次，每次换一个高度和角度，看完立刻缩回——绝不在同一位置长时间探头。真正移动时，绝不沿枪手的正对方向直线逃跑：要走Z字形，横穿射手视野的移动远比沿射击线纵向逃跑难命中。

points.en: Concealment tactics by terrain: at night, step into darkness or shadow and freeze — an assailant who cannot see you may not shoot, and random fire is unlikely to find you. In rural country, tall grass or a cornfield conceals day or night, provided you stay motionless so no swaying foliage or sound betrays you. Concealment is a pause to think, not a destination: analyse, then move toward real cover.
points.zh: 按地形用隐蔽物：夜间就退进黑暗或阴影里定住不动——看不见你的袭击者多半不会开枪，胡乱扫射也很难碰巧打中你。乡村地带，高草丛和玉米地昼夜都能藏身，前提是纹丝不动，别让摇晃的植株或声响出卖你。记住隐蔽只是喘息思考的间隙，不是终点：判断完形势，就向真正的掩体转移。

points.en: Someone blocking your path to the patient gets a script, not a shove: identify yourself, state you are there to help, tell them to move, and explain you cannot help the patient without access — remembering that keeping you away may be exactly what they want. If they yield, quietly have dispatch send police anyway; if they refuse, side-step and repeat the request. Open threats to summon police can inflame the confrontation.
points.zh: 有人挡在你和患者之间，用话术而不是推搡：表明身份、说明来意是救人、请对方让开，并解释见不到患者就没法救——同时心里清楚，拦住你可能正是对方的目的。对方让开了，也要悄悄让调度派警察过来备着；对方不让，就侧移一步再重复请求。公开叫嚣要喊警察，反而可能把冲突点燃。

points.en: The interview stance is your default posture with any stranger, above all in domestic encounters: about an arm's length away, body bladed 45 degrees to the person, feet shoulder-width, knees slightly bent, hands relaxed — a stance that looks conversational but is already a defensive position if violence erupts.
points.zh: 『会谈站姿』是你面对任何陌生人的默认姿势，家庭纠纷现场尤其如此：距对方约一臂远，身体侧转45度，双脚与肩同宽，膝盖微屈，双手放松——看着像在聊天，实际上已经是暴力突发时的防御架势。

points.en: Both grip breaks attack the thumb, the weak link of any hold. Wrist grab: fight the instinct to jerk backward against the fingers — locate the thumb and snap your forearm against it, usually pulling toward your own body, because one thumb is far weaker than four wrapped fingers. Shirt grab: seize the grabbing hand and twist it toward the thumb while flashing your free hand across the attacker's field of vision — the startle breaks their concentration and the grip loosens. Either way, once free you retreat; you do not counterattack.
points.zh: 两种挣脱术打的都是拇指——任何抓握的薄弱环节。被抓手腕：压住向后猛拽去对抗四根手指的本能——先找到拇指位置，把前臂朝拇指方向发力一抖，通常是往自己身体方向拉，因为一根拇指远弱于四指合围的握力。被抓衣襟：一手抓住对方抓你的手、朝拇指方向拧，同时另一只手在对方眼前猛地一晃——惊愕打断他的专注，抓力随之一松。无论哪种，挣开就撤，不恋战。

points.en: A shooter must complete a four-link chain — turn, locate, focus, fire — and distraction snaps it. Exploit the flinch reflex (the same blink you make when a passing car splashes your windshield): hurl your clipboard or a piece of kit at the assailant's face. The throw is the starting gun, not the plan — the instant the object leaves your hand, turn, get out of the line of fire, and sprint without waiting to see the reaction. Best destination is your vehicle, where you can radio for help or drive away; cut off from the ambulance, fall back on a cover-and-concealment survey of the ground around you.
points.zh: 开枪的人必须完成四步链条——转身、定位、聚焦、射击——而『分神』能掐断这根链条。利用人类的眨眼反射（就像会车时水花溅上挡风玻璃、明知打不到你也会眨眼那种本能）：把写字板或手边器材朝袭击者脸上掷过去。掷出物品只是发令枪，不是计划本身——东西一离手就立刻转身、脱离射击线、全力跑，不要留在原地看效果。首选目的地是自己的车，上车能呼救也能直接开走；被隔断回不了救护车时，就转入对周围地形的掩体与隐蔽物评估。

points.en: Force doctrine for paramedics: physical force is a defensive technique, never an aggressive move — defensive motions work as well as strikes and are far easier to justify against civil liability. The ceiling scales with the threat: when your life is in imminent danger, any action that gets you out of the situation counts as a reasonable level of force.
points.zh: 救护员的用力信条：肢体力量只用于防御，绝不用于进攻——防御性动作效果不输击打，而且面对民事追责时好辩护得多。力度上限随威胁浮动：当生命面临迫在眉睫的危险时，任何能让你脱身的动作都算合理限度的武力。

sections.titleEn: Crime Scenes: Treat the Patient, Spare the Evidence

points.en: The priority ladder at a violent crime scene, in order: your own safety, your partner's, the patient's, then bystanders' — followed by a duty to the whole community: keeping the scene intact raises the odds the suspect is caught and convicted.
points.zh: 暴力犯罪现场的优先级阶梯，依次是：自己的安全、搭档的安全、患者的安全、旁观者的安全——其后还有一层对整个社区的责任：现场保得越完整，嫌疑人被抓获并定罪的概率越高。

points.en: Two evidence types to name on the exam: testimonial evidence — a witness's oral account of the criminal act — and real (physical) evidence, which ties a suspect or victim to the crime through materials on the body, objects, and impressions.
points.zh: 考试要能点名的两类证据：言词证据（testimonial）——目击者对犯罪行为的口头陈述；实物证据（real/physical）——通过体表附着物、物件和印痕把嫌疑人或受害者与案件联系起来的证据。

points.en: Obey police parking and keep-out instructions without argument — the patch of pavement they wave you off may hold tire imprints, bullet casings, or blood. And cap the head-count: only the paramedics actually needed go inside.
points.zh: 对警方指定的停车位和禁入区不折不扣照办——他们让你绕开的那片地面，可能正压着轮胎印、弹壳或血迹。同时控制进场人数：只放真正需要动手的救护员进入现场。

points.en: The path of contamination is the designated walking route that keeps responders off the evidence — deliberately set away from the path the victim or suspect likely used, read off the ground from bloodstained areas, footwear impressions, and visible weapons, or already flagged by crews before you. First agency in? Hug the wall on your way to the patient: fleeing criminals take the shortest line out, so the wall route spares their exit path. Afterward, be ready to tell officers exactly where you walked, so your boot prints can be told apart from the victim's and suspect's footwear evidence.
points.zh: 『污染路径』是指定给应急人员走的那条路线，目的就是让脚印避开证据——它刻意避开受害者或嫌疑人最可能走过的路线，可以靠自己观察血迹区、鞋印、可见武器来判断，也可能已被先到的消防、救护或警察标定。你是第一支进场的队伍？那就贴着墙走向患者：逃离的罪犯几乎总走最短路线出门，贴墙走恰好避开他的逃离路径。事后要能向警察准确复述自己走过哪里，好让你的靴印与受害者、嫌疑人的鞋印证据区分开。

points.en: The crime-scene don't list: do not pick up expended cartridge casings to check the calibre; do not use the phones, flush the toilets, or run water in the sink — each act destroys evidence. When exposing a wound, cut around bullet holes, knife cuts, and tears, never through them; once clothing is off, do not shake it, or trace evidence and valuables rain out of the pockets. And whatever the resuscitation forced you to move, roll, or cut — tell law enforcement about every change your treatment made to the scene: patient care legitimately alters crime scenes; unreported alteration is what corrupts them.
points.zh: 犯罪现场的『不准清单』：不捡弹壳看口径；不用现场电话、不冲马桶、不开水龙头——每一样都会毁掉证据。剪衣暴露伤口时，绕开弹孔、刀口和撕裂处剪，绝不能从中间剪过去；脱下的衣物不要抖，一抖，口袋里的微量证据和贵重物品就撒了一地。凡是抢救过程迫使你挪动、翻转、剪开的东西，都要把这些改变如实告知警方：救治本身改变现场是正当的，不上报的改变才是对现场的污染。

points.en: You can be subpoenaed to give testimonial evidence about what you saw and heard, and the trial may be a year or more away — your written report is what will remember for you. Complete reports are the professional's mark; incomplete ones seldom keep anyone out of court.
points.zh: 你可能被传唤，就现场的所见所闻出庭作证，而开庭可能是一年甚至更久以后——到时替你记住细节的只有你写下的报告。完整的报告是专业救护员的标志；残缺的报告很少能让谁免于出庭。

points.en: Crime-scene documentation has three named pillars: what you saw, what you heard, and the chain of custody. 'Saw' means the scene as found — patient count, victim supine or prone, weapon location, overturned or damaged furniture, the position of every person present. 'Heard' goes beyond screams: arguing, a weapon being chambered or talk of using one, incriminating statements by anyone on scene, even a running television, alarm clock, or timer — each can anchor a timeline. Add any statements the patient makes during transport, and state facts only: no conclusions, no overstatement.
points.zh: 犯罪现场的文书有三根支柱：你看到了什么、你听到了什么、以及证据保管链。『看到的』指现场被发现时的原样——几名患者、受害者是仰卧还是俯卧、武器在哪个位置、有无翻倒或损坏的家具、现场每个人所处的位置。『听到的』远不止尖叫：争吵声、上膛声或扬言动武的话、在场任何人自证其罪的言语，甚至开着的电视、响着的闹钟或计时器——每一样都可能钉住案件的时间线。再补上患者转运途中说过的话，并且只写事实：不下结论，不夸大。

points.en: Disposition rules for the victim's effects: clothing stays with emergency department staff; weapons are secured by police whenever possible; medications travel to the ED with the patient; identification, wallet, or purse is best handed to law enforcement. And if the report is handwritten — print legibly.
points.zh: 受害者随身物品的去向规则：衣物留给急诊科工作人员；武器尽可能由警方收缴保管；药物随患者一起送急诊；身份证件、钱包、手提包最好直接交给警察。如果报告是手写的——请用清晰的印刷体。

points.en: One more habit from the chapter's case: when you withdraw from a hostile residence, back away facing the house — turn your back on someone who knows you are there, and you will never see the attack coming. Scene assessment is not a checkpoint but a process that runs until the call ends: a scene safe at entry can deteriorate with alarming speed.
points.zh: 本章案例留下的最后一个习惯：从充满敌意的住宅撤离时，要面朝房子倒退着走——对一个知道你在场的人转过身去，袭击来时你根本看不见。现场评估不是一次性的关卡，而是持续到出勤结束的过程：进门时安全的现场，可能以惊人的速度恶化。

atScene.en: Dispatched to a shooting, stabbing, or attempted suicide? Treat violence as expected, not possible — raise your guard before the wheels stop.
atScene.zh: 被派往枪击、捅刺或自杀未遂现场？把暴力当成必然而非可能——车还没停稳，警戒就该拉满。

atScene.en: Vehicle weapon stashes to eyeball during any car approach: glove box, top of the sun visor, arm rest, under either side of the seat, centre console, side-door pockets, and beside the driver's right thigh.
atScene.zh: 接近任何车辆时要扫视的藏武器点位：杂物箱、遮阳板上方、扶手、座椅两侧下方、中央扶手箱、车门侧袋，以及驾驶员右大腿旁。

atScene.en: Why youths join gangs — identity, respect, recognition, love, belonging, money, fear. Knowing the pull explains the patient in front of you; it never licenses you to imitate gang signs or slang.
atScene.zh: 青少年入帮派的七个动因——身份认同、尊重、被认可、爱、归属感、金钱、恐惧。理解这些拉力能帮你读懂眼前的患者，但绝不构成你模仿帮派手势或黑话的理由。

atScene.en: A vague 'injured person' call can hide anything from a picnic scrape to an intoxicated man with a rifle: have dispatch dig for details while you are en route — forewarned is forearmed — and stage in a safe spot if the picture stays murky.
atScene.zh: 一条语焉不详的『有人受伤』呼叫，背后可能是野餐擦伤，也可能是持步枪的醉汉：赶路途中让调度继续深挖信息——有备才能无患——情况始终不明就先在安全处staging。

atScene.en: Drive-by shooting victim: keep open-air treatment to the barest minimum and load fast — a patient visible on the pavement is the target the second volley comes back for.
atScene.zh: 驾车枪击的伤者：露天处置压到最少、快速装载上车——躺在路面上暴露的患者，正是第二轮扫射回头要找的靶子。

confusions.en: 'They can see I'm a paramedic, so they won't hurt me.' Assume anyone with a weapon will harm whoever is in sight — and your police-lookalike uniform can actively draw aggression meant for officers.
confusions.zh: 『他们看得出我是救护员，不会对我动手。』——错。要默认持武器者会伤害视线内的任何人，而你那身酷似警服的制服还会主动招来本冲着警察去的敌意。

confusions.en: Mistaking concealment for cover: a sofa, a drywall partition, a cinder-block wall, or a dark shadow hides you but stops nothing. Only mass that defeats bullets — engine block, brick, solid oak — counts as cover.
confusions.zh: 把隐蔽物错当掩体：沙发、石膏板隔墙、煤渣砖墙、暗影都只能藏住身影，一发子弹都挡不住。只有打不穿的实体——发动机缸体、砖墙、实心橡木——才算掩体。

confusions.en: 'Under the car, between the wheels, is the safest hiding spot.' A skilled shooter ricochets rounds off the pavement into that space — use the engine block and wheel areas, and stay clear of the fuel tank.
confusions.zh: 『钻到车底两轮之间最安全。』——老练的射手能让子弹在路面上跳弹打进车底。正确做法是利用发动机缸体和车轮部位，并远离油箱。

confusions.en: 'Retreating means abandoning my patient.' Retreat is the professional standard, not cowardice: a paramedic who rushes in and gets hurt becomes one more casualty, and disciplined awareness makes care safer, not slower.
confusions.zh: 『撤退就是抛弃患者。』——撤退是职业标准，不是怯懦：贸然冲入而受伤的救护员只会变成又一名伤员；有纪律的警觉让救治更安全，而不是更慢。

confusions.en: 'Evidence is the police's problem.' Every step, cut, and moved object of yours changes the scene. Patient care legitimately alters crime scenes — alteration you fail to report is what corrupts them.
confusions.zh: 『证据是警察的事。』——你的每一个脚印、每一剪刀、每一次挪动都在改变现场。救治正当地改变现场；你没有上报的改变才是对现场的污染。

confusions.en: 'Once I reach the patient, the scene is settled.' Scene assessment runs until the call ends — a scene safe at entry can deteriorate with alarming speed, and tunnel vision on the patient is how crews get blindsided.
confusions.zh: 『见到患者，现场这关就算过了。』——现场评估要持续到出勤结束：进门时安全的现场可能以惊人的速度恶化，而对患者的『隧道视野』正是团队被偷袭的根源。

confusions.en: 'A hostage should look for a chance to escape.' The opposite: a failed attempt worsens every hostage's position, and your survival odds climb with time — staying calm, inconspicuous, and useful is the strategy.
confusions.zh: 『被劫为人质就该找机会逃跑。』——恰恰相反：一次失败的尝试会让所有人质处境更糟，而你的生存几率随时间上升——冷静、低调、让自己有用，才是策略。

mnemonics.name: 帮派 3R
mnemonics.en: Gang culture runs on three Rs: Reputation (earned by crime), Respect (often really fear), Retaliation (mandatory after any 'diss').
mnemonics.zh: 帮派文化的三个R：Reputation 名声（靠犯罪挣）、Respect 尊重（实为恐惧）、Retaliation 报复（被『不敬』后必然发生）。

mnemonics.name: 开枪四步链
mnemonics.en: A shooter must Turn, Locate, Focus, Fire — throw a distraction into any link and the chain breaks long enough for you to run.
mnemonics.zh: 射手必须完成『转身—定位—聚焦—射击』四步；往任何一环里砸进一个『分神』，链条就断开，够你逃出射击线。

mnemonics.name: 两个C
mnemonics.en: Cover is Concrete — it stops bullets. Concealment is a Curtain — it only blocks the view.
mnemonics.zh: Cover 是混凝土——挡得住子弹；Concealment 是窗帘——只挡得住视线。

mnemonics.name: 安全四序
mnemonics.en: Crime-scene safety priority: me, my partner, my patient, the public — in that order, then the community's evidence.
mnemonics.zh: 犯罪现场的安全次序：先自己、再搭档、然后患者、最后旁观者——之后才轮到属于整个社区的证据。

selfCheck.qEn: You are first on scene to a 'man slumped over the wheel.' How do you park, and why?
selfCheck.qZh: 你首车到达『有人趴在方向盘上』的现场，救护车怎么停？为什么？
selfCheck.aEn: At least 6 m behind the vehicle, angled 10 degrees toward the driver's side facing the shoulder, front wheels turned fully left — so the wheels and engine block shield you against gunfire from the car.
selfCheck.aZh: 停在目标车后方至少6米、向驾驶侧偏10度、车头朝路肩、前轮向左打死——让车轮和发动机缸体挡住可能从车内射来的子弹。

selfCheck.qEn: Cover versus concealment — define both and give three examples of each.
selfCheck.qZh: 掩体与隐蔽物——各下定义并各举三例。
selfCheck.aEn: Cover stops bullets: engine block, brick or concrete-block wall, solid oak desk (also refrigerators, curbs, dumpsters, ground depressions). Concealment only hides you: tall grass, shrubbery, dark shadow (also sofas and stud-and-drywall interior walls).
selfCheck.aZh: 掩体挡得住子弹：发动机缸体、砖墙/混凝土砌块墙、实心橡木桌（还有冰箱、路缘石、垃圾大箱、地面凹陷）。隐蔽物只藏得住身影：高草、灌木、暗影（还有沙发、龙骨石膏板隔墙）。

selfCheck.qEn: First agency into a crime scene: what route do you walk to the patient, and why?
selfCheck.qZh: 你是第一支进入犯罪现场的队伍：走什么路线到患者身边？为什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Along the wall. Fleeing criminals almost always take the shortest straight line out, so the wall route avoids contaminating the exit path — and afterward you tell police exactly where you walked so your prints can be ruled out.
selfCheck.aZh: 贴着墙走。逃离的罪犯几乎总走最短的直线出门，贴墙路线正好避开其逃离路径不受污染——事后再向警方准确复述你走过哪里，好把你的脚印排除掉。

selfCheck.qEn: Evidence rules when cutting clothing off a shooting or stabbing victim?
selfCheck.qZh: 为枪伤或刀伤患者剪开衣物时的证据规则是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Cut around bullet holes, knife cuts, and tears — never through them; do not shake removed clothing (trace evidence falls from pockets); leave clothing with ED staff; and report every treatment-caused change to police.
selfCheck.aZh: 绕开弹孔、刀口和撕裂处剪，绝不从中间剪过去；脱下的衣物不要抖（口袋里的微量证据会掉落）；衣物留给急诊科工作人员；救治造成的每一处现场改变都要告知警方。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the three pillars of crime-scene documentation. Who should receive the victim's wallet and ID?
selfCheck.qZh: 犯罪现场文书的三大支柱是什么？受害者的钱包和证件应交给谁？
selfCheck.aEn: What you saw, what you heard, and the chain of custody. ID, wallet, or purse goes to law enforcement; medications travel with the patient to the ED; weapons are secured by police whenever possible.
selfCheck.aZh: 你看到了什么、你听到了什么、证据保管链。证件、钱包、手提包最好交给警方；药物随患者送急诊；武器尽可能由警方收缴保管。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Shooting and stabbing calls: BC's explicit MOI documentation checklist
bcAlerts.topicZh: 枪击与捅刺呼叫：BC 明列的受伤机制文书清单
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook teaches the general documentation frame — what you saw, what you heard, chain of custody — without a fixed item list for penetrating trauma.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材只给出通用文书框架——所见、所闻、证据保管链——对穿透伤没有固定的记录条目清单。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's exam guidelines spell out exactly what to record. Shooting: type of firearm, range, angle of shot, type of bullet if possible, entrance and exit wounds, patient's initial position and condition, loss of consciousness. Stabbing: type of weapon/object, its length and width, slashed versus stabbed, number of wounds, other injuries, initial position and condition, loss of consciousness. Gather these by observation and bystander report — never by handling the weapon.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 考试指南明确列出必记项。枪击：枪支类型、射击距离、射击角度、可能的话记子弹类型、入口与出口伤、患者最初的位置与状态、有无意识丧失。捅刺：凶器/物体类型、其长度与宽度、划伤还是刺伤、伤口数量、其他损伤、最初位置与状态、有无意识丧失。这些信息靠观察和旁观者陈述获取——绝不靠上手摆弄武器。
bcAlerts.ref: EMALB BC Provincial Examination Guidelines p.13（Current to June 15, 2026）
